clue.text: Crime discovered by detectives following one into house

indicators.note: into says the detectives-and-one group goes inside the word for house

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: following puts the detectives after the one in the inserted run

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Police find a murder after entering a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals insertion and 'following' fixes the order of the inserted pair; 'discovered' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing another person is the gravest crime on the statute book.

clue.text: It comes in term-time and gives rise to mirth

indicators.note: comes in means the word it is placed inside the term's name

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford University and in the English law courts

explanation.surface: Laughter breaks out during the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the January-to-March term at Oxford University and in the English law courts; 'comes in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud merriment and laughter.

clue.text: Get pickled, notice, after our time in jolly surroundings

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Get pickled, notice, after our time in jolly surroundings (9)' for MARINADED: AD (notice) and AD (our time) inside MARINE (jolly) give at most MARINADE, eight letters; no reading supplies the final D, and the scan confirms the text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Get pickled, notice, after our time in jolly surroundings

clue.text: Creature caught by decoy put in trap

indicators.note: caught by means the creature is held inside the following words

explanation.surface: An animal is lured into a trap with a decoy.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'decoy put'.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Concluded notes about Italian leader

indicators.note: about means the musical notes go round the Italian title

parts.note: D, E and D are notes of the musical scale
Il Duce, 'the leader', was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Someone wrote memos about Mussolini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the notes go round the title; Il Duce was Mussolini.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reason out, so deduced means worked out or inferred.

clue.text: Approval as expressed by one of the Trinity boatmen

explanation.surface: Someone cheers on a rowing crew from a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By George!' is an exclamation of approving surprise; the 'Trinity boatmen' are the three men of Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat, not a Trinity College crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'by George' voices hearty approval, and George is one of the three friends who row up the Thames in Jerome's comic novel.

clue.text: A single ship's deserter in river gets clear

indicators.note: in puts the single and the deserter inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a single is one
rats are said to desert a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A lone sailor who jumped ship hides in a river and is acquitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to free them from blame.

clue.text: Search for a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone hunts around for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a drawer is to ransack it; a rifle is a long-barrelled gun.

clue.text: "When' I am grown to man's " (R.L. Stevenson)

definitions.text: "When' I am grown to man's " (R.L. Stevenson)

parts.words: "When' I am grown to man's " (R.L. Stevenson)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word ends the first line of Stevenson's poem Looking Forward

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from 'Looking Forward' in A Child's Garden of Verses: 'When I am grown to man's ___, I shall be very proud and great'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach man's full standing or condition means to be grown up; this sense of condition or rank is the old meaning used here.

clue.text: Comments by players — of the first elevens?

explanation.surface: Players remark on who made the top teams.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A SIDES it means first teams, as in a club's first eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors address remarks to the audience unheard by other characters; the top teams of a club are its A teams.

clue.text: Carrier with flier right in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle says the letter for right sits at the centre of the bird's name

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot, a flier

explanation.surface: An airline with a pilot sitting centrally in the cockpit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier' suggests an airline alongside 'flier'; it is a goods vehicle, and the flier is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A goods vehicle carries freight by road, so it is a carrier.

clue.text: Record order apt to cause embarrassment

parts.note: a record is a disc
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
apt means fit, suitable

explanation.surface: Ordering the wrong record could be embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit someone is to unsettle and fluster them, making them uneasy.

clue.text: Lightweight in split gave up title

indicators.note: in places the light weight inside the word for split

parts.note: rend means tear apart, split
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A lightweight boxer, after a split decision, relinquished his belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the insertion. 'Lightweight' and 'title' suggest boxing, but the weight is a unit of measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally relinquishing a claim or rank is renouncing it.

clue.text: First Lady books for sporting contest

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: The President's wife reserves seats for a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife; here it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A single competition at a sports meeting is called an event.

clue.text: Walked when young shaver showed the way

parts.note: Sweeney Todd, the murderous barber of Fleet Street
led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: A small boy walked ahead of the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young shaver' looks like a phrase for a boy; 'young' belongs to the definition and the shaver is the barber Sweeney Todd.
explanation.definitionFit: Toddlers totter about on unsteady legs as small children first learning to walk.

clue.text: Circus performer in Rome Latin version

indicators.note: version means a new rendering of the letters, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A circus act appears in a Latin translation in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges ROME and LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A big-cat trainer performs with lions in the circus ring.

clue.text: I'm not going to say why it is sung

parts.note: I shan't is a refusal: I'm not going to

indicators.note: say means the following word is spoken, so its sound gives a letter

parts.note: the spoken word why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to explain the reason for a song.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAN'T plus the letter Y, which is said 'why'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea shanties are work songs sailors sang while hauling ropes.

clue.text: Covenant to supply cricketers without a square

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the cricketers go round the a

parts.note: Test men are players chosen for international Test matches
a T-square is a drawing tool, giving T

explanation.surface: An agreement to provide players for a match, minus a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, the old sense; a T-square is a drafting tool. 'square' suggests a cricket square, the pitch area.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament, as in the Old and New Testaments, is a solemn covenant or agreement.

clue.text: It may be felt in a liner

definitions.text: It may be felt in a liner

parts.words: It may be felt in a liner
parts.note: felt is the material, not the past of feel; a liner is a lining laid under carpet

explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' looks like sensed and 'liner' like a ship; felt is the padding fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding of felt or rubber is laid beneath carpet to cushion it.

clue.text: Neighbour involves little woman in a row

indicators.note: in places the little woman inside the a-and-row pair

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A neighbour drags a young woman into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' recalls Louisa May Alcott's Little Women, whose heroine is Jo; 'Neighbour' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something is to lie next to it, sharing a border.

clue.text: Delicacy in NE City redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment means the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gourmet treat in a regenerated city in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redevelopment' rearranges NE CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine distinction or a subtle detail is a delicacy of judgment.

clue.text: Squashes a relative

explanation.surface: Someone flattens a member of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer is a phrasal verb for treading on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading heavily on something crushes it flat; a spouse's son from an earlier marriage is kin by marriage.

clue.text: Chastise the cat, possibly

explanation.surface: Punish the family pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat here is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip once used for flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate severely is to flog; a whip such as the cat-o'-nine-tails is a lash.

clue.text: Minister provides remedy without a word of thanks in return

indicators.note: without means outside, so the remedy surrounds the thanks

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

indicators.note: in return means the word of thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers a cure without even being thanked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' reverses the thanks and 'without' means outside. Ta is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England is a minister of religion.

clue.text: One left in dark

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: A single person is left in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with no lamps burning is dark.

clue.text: Fifty soldiers turned up with the King afterwards

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the soldiers are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Fifty soldiers arrived with the monarch afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns TA into AT. ER usually means the Queen; here it is Edward Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Drink which may be barred

explanation.surface: A drink that might be banned in some places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' suggests forbidden; it means made into bars, as confectionery is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot cocoa is a drink, and the same sweet is sold moulded in bars.

clue.text: This girl sounds a droop

explanation.surface: A girl's name has a sad, drooping sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds a droop' means is said like 'a drupe', a stone fruit, which this fruit is; the first sense is a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's name, and the fruit of the Mediterranean tree is a drupe, a fleshy fruit with a stone.

clue.text: It provides in-flight reading matter

parts.note: the reading meant is not a magazine but a dial reading on an aircraft instrument showing height

explanation.walkthrough: 'reading matter' suggests magazines handed out on a plane; the reading is the figure on a cockpit gauge.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft instrument that displays height above sea level gives a reading throughout a flight.

clue.text: Lad that is moved to perfection

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A young man is emotionally stirred to reach perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges LAD plus IE (i.e.).
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect model or standard to aim at is called an ideal.

clue.text: Fears loss of opener to slips

indicators.note: loss of opener means the first letter of the word for fears is dropped

parts.note: terrors are fears

explanation.surface: A batting side fears losing its opening batsman to catches in the slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' and 'slips' suggest cricket: an opening batsman caught by fielders in the slips. Here the opener is the first letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, so slips are mistakes.

clue.text: Money held in trust not long ago

indicators.note: held in says the money sits inside the word for trust

parts.note: rely means trust, depend
a cent is a coin, money

explanation.surface: Funds were placed in a trust a short while back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trust' looks like a fund holding money; it is a verb, and 'held in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened lately happened a short time back.
